topics.definition: SQL (Structured Query Language) is used to create, retrieve, update and manage data in relational databases.
tips: SQL is the standard language for relational databases.

topics.definition: DDL (Data Definition Language) defines and modifies database objects.
topics.example: CREATE TABLE Student(ID INT, Name VARCHAR(50));

topics.definition: DML (Data Manipulation Language) inserts, updates and deletes records.
DCL (Data Control Language) controls user permissions.
topics.example: GRANT SELECT ON Student TO user1;

topics.definition: Joins combine rows from two or more tables.
topics.syntax: INNER JOIN, LEFT JOIN, RIGHT JOIN, FULL JOIN
topics.example: SELECT * FROM Student INNER JOIN Course ON Student.ID=Course.ID;
tips: INNER JOIN is the most commonly used join.

topics.definition: Aggregate functions perform calculations on groups of rows.
GROUP BY groups rows sharing the same values.
topics.syntax: SELECT Dept, COUNT(*) FROM Employee GROUP BY Dept;

topics.definition: ORDER BY sorts query results in ascending or descending order.
topics.syntax: SELECT * FROM Student ORDER BY Name ASC;
tips: ASC is default; DESC sorts in descending order.
